correctness.rationale: The proof uses the nondegenerate trace pairing on sl2 in every odd characteristic; any nonzero A has centralizer kA and image A^perp. For nonzero first target Z, there are q(q^2-1) first-coefficient pairs and q^3 second-coefficient lifts per prescribed W. For Z=0, commuting pairs are partitioned by a unique projective line; q+1 or q^2+q+1 lines lie in W^perp depending on W, with q^4 lifts per pair and a q^6 zero-pair correction. The resulting values sum to q^12. The adjoint-rank result follows by solving centralizer equations. Exhaustive q=3 all-target tests and q=5 three-stratum tests independently corroborate the formulas. A separate full direct-bracket multiplication census of 531441 pairs at q=3 independently confirmed all 729 target-fiber sizes.

value.rationale: The bracket-fiber distribution is an intrinsic, motivated finite-field invariant of the first Takiff extension of a simple Lie algebra; it refines mere bracket surjectivity or commuting probability and separates all target strata in a nonsemisimple six-dimensional algebra. The uniformity on nonzero projection fibers and the jump on its abelian ideal are structural facts not implicit in a generic orbit dimension. The exact count applies simultaneously to every odd prime power and yields an explicit measure of pair commutativity. This is more than an arbitrary numerical slice, though not claimed as a general Takiff-order theorem.
